parts.label: a
hints: At any branch split, the probabilities leaving the node must sum to 1: $P(E) + P(E') = 1$.
For independent events along a path, multiply the branch probabilities: $P(E \cap E) = P(E) \times P(E)$.

walkthrough.text:
Find the complement probability at the first node:
$$P(E') = 1 - P(E) = 1 - 0.68 = 0.32$$

Multiply along the path $(E, E)$:
$$P(E \cap E) = 0.68 \times 0.68 = 0.4624$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Apply the node sum rule where outgoing probabilities must total 1:
$$P(E') = 1 - 0.68 = 0.32$$

Multiply along the desired path for independent trials:
$$P(E \cap E) = 0.68 \times 0.68 = 0.4624 = \frac{289}{625}$$

parts.label: a
hints: The three outgoing branches from the node must add up to 1: $P(L) + P(S) + P(R) = 1$.
Since Straight and Right are equally likely, divide the remaining probability $1 - 0.40 = 0.60$ by 2.

walkthrough.text:
Compute the probability for the Straight branch:
$$P(S) = \frac{1 - 0.40}{2} = \frac{0.60}{2} = 0.30$$

Multiply along the path $(L, R)$:
$$P(L \cap R) = 0.40 \times 0.30 = 0.12$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Partition the remaining probability equally between the two symmetric branches:
$$P(S) = P(R) = \frac{1 - 0.40}{2} = 0.30$$

Traverse the sequence of two independent decisions by multiplying branch values:
$$P(L \text{ then } R) = 0.40 \times 0.30 = 0.12 = \frac{3}{25}$$

parts.label: a
hints: Without replacement, the total number of markers drops from 8 to 7 on the second draw.
If a red marker was removed, the number of red markers decreases to 4 while blue markers remain 3.

walkthrough.text:
Update the contents after removing one red marker:
$$P(\text{Blue}_2 \mid \text{Red}_1) = \frac{3}{7}$$

Multiply branch probabilities along the path $(\text{Red}, \text{Red})$:
$$P(\text{Red}_1 \cap \text{Red}_2) = \frac{5}{8} \times \frac{4}{7} = \frac{20}{56} = \frac{5}{14}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Adjust the sample space composition after the first red draw:
$$\text{Remaining: 4 Red, 3 Blue (Total 7)} \implies P(B_2 \mid R_1) = \frac{3}{7}$$

Compute the joint path probability using the multiplication rule:
$$P(R_1 \cap R_2) = \frac{5}{8} \times \frac{4}{7} = \frac{5}{14} \approx 0.357$$

ai_rubric.observable: State P(Blue on 2nd | Red on 1st) = 3/7 and formulate P(Red, Red) = (5/8) * (4/7).

parts.label: a
hints: Find the probability of Wednesday being Wet from the Dry Tuesday condition: $P(W \mid D) = 0.25$.
Find the complement probability for Thursday being Dry given Wednesday is Wet: $1 - 0.60 = 0.40$.

walkthrough.text:
Identify the conditional branch probabilities:
$$P(W_{\text{Wed}} \mid D_{\text{Tue}}) = 0.25, \quad P(D_{\text{Thu}} \mid W_{\text{Wed}}) = 1 - 0.60 = 0.40$$

Multiply along the path $(W_{\text{Wed}}, D_{\text{Thu}})$:
$$P(W_{\text{Wed}} \cap D_{\text{Thu}}) = 0.25 \times 0.40 = 0.10$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Determine the state transition values for both successive days:
$$P(\text{Wed Wet}) = 0.25, \quad P(\text{Thu Dry} \mid \text{Wed Wet}) = 1 - 0.60 = 0.40$$

Evaluate the path probability by multiplying sequential branches:
$$P(\text{Wet then Dry}) = 0.25 \times 0.40 = 0.10 = \frac{1}{10}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identify transition probabilities P(Wed Wet | Tue Dry) = 0.25 and P(Thu Dry | Wed Wet) = 1 - 0.60 = 0.40.

parts.label: a
hints: Exactly one Head corresponds to two distinct paths: $(H, T)$ and $(T, H)$.
Multiply branch probabilities along each path and add the results.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the probabilities of the two valid paths:
$$P(H, T) = 0.7 \times 0.3 = 0.21, \quad P(T, H) = 0.3 \times 0.7 = 0.21$$

Sum the probabilities of the mutually exclusive paths:
$$P(\text{exactly one Head}) = 0.21 + 0.21 = 0.42$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Identify the two separate paths meeting the condition of exactly one Head:
$$\text{Paths: } (H, T) \text{ and } (T, H)$$

Sum the independent path multiplications:
$$P = (0.7 \times 0.3) + (0.3 \times 0.7) = 0.21 + 0.21 = 0.42$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identify the two mutually exclusive paths (H, T) and (T, H) and calculate (0.7 * 0.3) + (0.3 * 0.7).

parts.label: a
hints: An outcome that cannot happen is assigned a probability of 0 on a tree diagram branch.
The only path that can yield a bonus is $(\text{Red}, \text{Bonus})$.

walkthrough.text:
State the probability for the impossible branch:
$$P(\text{Bonus} \mid \text{Blue}) = 0$$

Calculate the total probability along the only valid path:
$$P(\text{Bonus}) = P(\text{Red}) \times P(\text{Bonus} \mid \text{Red}) = 0.6 \times \frac{1}{6} = 0.1$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Recognize that impossible branches carry zero probability:
$$P(\text{Bonus} \mid \text{Blue}) = 0$$

Evaluate the single active branch path yielding the bonus:
$$P(\text{Bonus}) = 0.6 \times \frac{1}{6} = 0.1 = \frac{1}{10}$$

ai_rubric.observable: State that the probability of scoring a bonus after Blue is 0 (impossible branch).
Calculate the overall probability of scoring a bonus as 0.6 * (1/6) = 0.1 (or 1/10).

parts.label: a
hints: On the first draw, the probability of selecting silver is $4/6$.
After taking one silver coin, 3 silver coins remain out of 5 total coins.

walkthrough.text:
Set up the conditional product along the silver-silver branch:
$$P(S_1 \cap S_2) = P(S_1) \times P(S_2 \mid S_1) = \frac{4}{6} \times \frac{3}{5}$$

Simplify the resulting fraction:
$$P(S_1 \cap S_2) = \frac{12}{30} = \frac{2}{5} = 0.4$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Formulate the branch probabilities for two sequential draws without replacement:
$$P(S_1) = \frac{4}{6}, \quad P(S_2 \mid S_1) = \frac{3}{5}$$

Multiply along the path to evaluate the joint probability:
$$P(S_1 \cap S_2) = \frac{4}{6} \times \frac{3}{5} = \frac{2}{5}$$

parts.label: b
hints: Different metals means either (Silver then Gold) or (Gold then Silver).
Calculate the probability of each path and sum them.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the probability for each path of different metals:
$$P(S, G) = \frac{4}{6} \times \frac{2}{5} = \frac{8}{30}, \quad P(G, S) = \frac{2}{6} \times \frac{4}{5} = \frac{8}{30}$$

Add the mutually exclusive path probabilities:
$$P(\text{different}) = \frac{8}{30} + \frac{8}{30} = \frac{16}{30} = \frac{8}{15}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Identify the two mutually exclusive branch sequences yielding different metals:
$$\text{Paths: } (S_1, G_2) \text{ and } (G_1, S_2)$$

Add their path products:
$$P = \left(\frac{4}{6} \times \frac{2}{5}\right) + \left(\frac{2}{6} \times \frac{4}{5}\right) = \frac{8}{30} + \frac{8}{30} = \frac{16}{30} = \frac{8}{15} \approx 0.533$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identify and sum the probabilities of the two paths (S, G) and (G, S): (4/6 * 2/5) + (2/6 * 4/5).

parts.label: a
hints: Find the complement probability for no dessert following Pasta: $1 - 0.35 = 0.65$.
Multiply along the path: $P(P \cap D') = P(P) \times P(D' \mid P)$.

walkthrough.text:
Find the conditional probability of not taking dessert after choosing pasta:
$$P(D' \mid P) = 1 - 0.35 = 0.65$$

Multiply along the branch path $(P, D')$:
$$P(P \cap D') = 0.60 \times 0.65 = 0.39$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Determine the branch value for the complement outcome following pasta:
$$P(D' \mid P) = 1 - P(D \mid P) = 1 - 0.35 = 0.65$$

Traverse the path by taking the product of the branch probabilities:
$$P(P \cap D') = 0.60 \times 0.65 = 0.39 = \frac{39}{100}$$

parts.label: b
hints: Students can take dessert through two routes: choosing Pasta then Dessert, or choosing Rice then Dessert.
The probability of choosing Rice is $1 - 0.60 = 0.40$.

walkthrough.text:
Determine the two routes leading to dessert:
$$P(P \cap D) = 0.60 \times 0.35 = 0.21, \quad P(R \cap D) = (1 - 0.60) \times 0.55 = 0.40 \times 0.55 = 0.22$$

Sum both branch path probabilities:
$$P(D) = 0.21 + 0.22 = 0.43$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Identify the complementary main course probability:
$$P(R) = 1 - 0.60 = 0.40$$

Formulate the total probability sum across both meal paths:
$$P(D) = P(P)P(D \mid P) + P(R)P(D \mid R) = (0.60 \times 0.35) + (0.40 \times 0.55)$$

Sum the path values to find the total probability:
$$P(D) = 0.21 + 0.22 = 0.43$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identify P(Rice) = 1 - 0.60 = 0.40 and the two paths leading to dessert: (Pasta, Dessert) and (Rice, Dessert).
Calculate the sum of path probabilities: (0.60 * 0.35) + (0.40 * 0.55).

parts.label: a
hints: First find the probability of losing match 1: $P(L_1) = 1 - 0.65 = 0.35$.
Next find the probability of losing match 2 given she lost match 1: $1 - 0.30 = 0.70$.
Multiply along the path: $P(L_1 \cap L_2) = P(L_1) \times P(L_2 \mid L_1)$.

walkthrough.text:
Find the complement probabilities for each stage:
$$P(L_1) = 1 - 0.65 = 0.35, \quad P(L_2 \mid L_1) = 1 - 0.30 = 0.70$$

Multiply along the loss-loss path:
$$P(L_1 \cap L_2) = 0.35 \times 0.70 = 0.245$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Evaluate the complement values for the first match and the subsequent conditioned match:
$$P(L_1) = 1 - 0.65 = 0.35, \quad P(L_2 \mid L_1) = 1 - 0.30 = 0.70$$

Traverse the lower branch path by computing the product:
$$P(L_1 \cap L_2) = 0.35 \times 0.70 = 0.245 = \frac{49}{200}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identify P(Loss 1) = 1 - 0.65 = 0.35 and P(Loss 2 | Loss 1) = 1 - 0.30 = 0.70, and calculate 0.35 * 0.70.

parts.label: b
hints: Winning exactly one match corresponds to the paths $(W_1, L_2)$ and $(L_1, W_2)$.
For $(W_1, L_2)$, the second branch probability is $1 - 0.80 = 0.20$.
Add the probabilities of both paths: $P(W_1, L_2) + P(L_1, W_2)$.

walkthrough.text:
Compute the probability of winning the first match and losing the second:
$$P(W_1 \cap L_2) = 0.65 \times (1 - 0.80) = 0.65 \times 0.20 = 0.13$$

Compute the probability of losing the first match and winning the second:
$$P(L_1 \cap W_2) = (1 - 0.65) \times 0.30 = 0.35 \times 0.30 = 0.105$$

Sum the mutually exclusive path values:
$$P(\text{exactly one win}) = 0.13 + 0.105 = 0.235$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Calculate the path probability for a win followed by a loss:
$$P(W_1 \cap L_2) = 0.65 \times 0.20 = 0.13$$

Calculate the path probability for a loss followed by a win:
$$P(L_1 \cap W_2) = 0.35 \times 0.30 = 0.105$$

Add the two disjoint path probabilities:
$$P = 0.13 + 0.105 = 0.235 = \frac{47}{200}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identify the two mutually exclusive paths: (Win 1, Loss 2) and (Loss 1, Win 2).

parts.label: a
hints: Draw or visualize a tree diagram with three initial branches for $B$, $C$, and $W$.
Multiply each transport mode probability by its corresponding conditional probability of being late.
Sum the three path products to obtain the overall probability: $P(L) = P(B \cap L) + P(C \cap L) + P(W \cap L)$.

walkthrough.text:
Formulate the total probability across all three transport paths:
$$P(L) = P(B)P(L \mid B) + P(C)P(L \mid C) + P(W)P(L \mid W)$$

Calculate each individual path probability:
$$P(B \cap L) = 0.50 \times 0.10 = 0.050, \quad P(C \cap L) = 0.30 \times 0.05 = 0.015, \quad P(W \cap L) = 0.20 \times 0.25 = 0.050$$

Add the three path values together:
$$P(L) = 0.050 + 0.015 + 0.050 = 0.115$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Express the overall probability of being late as the sum of three disjoint paths:
$$P(L) = \sum_{m \in \{B, C, W\}} P(m) P(L \mid m)$$

Substitute the branch probabilities for each route:
$$P(L) = (0.50 \times 0.10) + (0.30 \times 0.05) + (0.20 \times 0.25)$$

Sum the numerical products to find the final value:
$$P(L) = 0.050 + 0.015 + 0.050 = 0.115 = \frac{23}{200}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Set up the total probability sum across all three transport branches: P(B)P(L | B) + P(C)P(L | C) + P(W)P(L | W).

parts.label: b
hints: Arriving on time is the complement of arriving late: $P(L') = 1 - P(L)$.
For the conditional probability, the restricted sample space is $P(C \cup W) = 0.30 + 0.20 = 0.50$.
The favourable outcomes in this restricted space are late arrivals by bicycle or walking: $0.015 + 0.050 = 0.065$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the probability of arriving on time using the complement:
$$P(\text{On time}) = 1 - P(L) = 1 - 0.115 = 0.885$$

Calculate the numerator and denominator for the conditional probability:
$$P((C \cup W) \cap L) = 0.015 + 0.050 = 0.065, \quad P(C \cup W) = 0.30 + 0.20 = 0.50$$

Evaluate the conditional fraction:
$$P(L \mid (C \cup W)) = \frac{0.065}{0.50} = 0.13$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Apply the complement rule to obtain the on-time probability:
$$P(L') = 1 - 0.115 = 0.885 = \frac{177}{200}$$

Set up the conditional probability definition for the subset condition:
$$P(L \mid C \cup W) = \frac{P(L \cap (C \cup W))}{P(C \cup W)} = \frac{0.015 + 0.050}{0.30 + 0.20}$$

Divide to find the exact conditional rate:
$$P(L \mid C \cup W) = \frac{0.065}{0.50} = 0.13 = \frac{13}{100}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Formulate conditional probability P((C or W) and Late) / P(C or W) = (0.015 + 0.050) / (0.30 + 0.20).

parts.label: a
hints: Box $P$ gives a Red marble with probability $3/5$ and a Yellow marble with probability $2/5$.
When a marble is added to Box $Q$, its total count increases from 8 to 9.
Multiply each transfer probability by the probability of drawing Red from Box $Q$ and sum the results.

walkthrough.text:
Determine the composition of Box $Q$ after each transfer:
$$\text{If Red moved: } 5R, 4Y \text{ (total 9)}; \quad \text{If Yellow moved: } 4R, 5Y \text{ (total 9)}$$

Formulate the total probability of selecting Red from Box $Q$:
$$P(R_Q) = \left(\frac{3}{5} \times \frac{5}{9}\right) + \left(\frac{2}{5} \times \frac{4}{9}\right)$$

Sum the path probabilities:
$$P(R_Q) = \frac{15}{45} + \frac{8}{45} = \frac{23}{45}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Update the sample space in Box $Q$ conditioned on the transferred marble colour:
$$\text{Condition } R_P: P(R_Q \mid R_P) = \frac{5}{9}, \quad \text{Condition } Y_P: P(R_Q \mid Y_P) = \frac{4}{9}$$

Apply the law of total probability using the branch probabilities from Box $P$:
$$P(R_Q) = P(R_P)P(R_Q \mid R_P) + P(Y_P)P(R_Q \mid Y_P) = \left(\frac{3}{5} \times \frac{5}{9}\right) + \left(\frac{2}{5} \times \frac{4}{9}\right)$$

Evaluate the resulting sum:
$$P(R_Q) = \frac{15 + 8}{45} = \frac{23}{45} \approx 0.511$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identify updated contents of Box Q: if Red transferred, 5 red and 4 yellow (total 9); if Yellow transferred, 4 red and 5 yellow (total 9).

parts.label: b
hints: The two marbles are of the same colour if both are Red or both are Yellow.
For both Yellow: $P(Y_P) = 2/5$, and in Box $Q$ there are now 5 yellow marbles out of 9.
Sum the two path probabilities: $P(R_P \cap R_Q) + P(Y_P \cap Y_Q)$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the probability of transferring Red and drawing Red:
$$P(R_P \cap R_Q) = \frac{3}{5} \times \frac{5}{9} = \frac{15}{45}$$

Calculate the probability of transferring Yellow and drawing Yellow:
$$P(Y_P \cap Y_Q) = \frac{2}{5} \times \frac{5}{9} = \frac{10}{45}$$

Sum the two mutually exclusive path probabilities:
$$P(\text{same colour}) = \frac{15}{45} + \frac{10}{45} = \frac{25}{45} = \frac{5}{9}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Calculate the first matching path product where both items are red:
$$P(R_P \cap R_Q) = \frac{3}{5} \times \frac{5}{9} = \frac{15}{45}$$

Calculate the second matching path product where both items are yellow:
$$P(Y_P \cap Y_Q) = \frac{2}{5} \times \frac{5}{9} = \frac{10}{45}$$

Add the two disjoint path probabilities together:
$$P = \frac{15 + 10}{45} = \frac{25}{45} = \frac{5}{9} \approx 0.556$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identify the two matching paths: (Red from P, Red from Q) and (Yellow from P, Yellow from Q).

parts.label: a
hints: Identify Monday Sunny probability: $P(S_M) = 0.70$.
From the Sunny node on Monday, read the branch for Tuesday being Sunny: $0.80$.
Multiply along the branch: $P(S_M \cap S_T) = P(S_M) \times P(S_T \mid S_M)$.
Compute $0.70 \times 0.80 = 0.56$.

walkthrough.text:
Identify the relevant branch values:
$$P(S_M) = 0.70, \quad P(S_T \mid S_M) = 0.80$$

Multiply along the branch path $(S_M, S_T)$:
$$P(S_M \cap S_T) = 0.70 \times 0.80 = 0.56$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Extract the initial state probability and the transition probability:
$$P(S_M) = 0.70, \quad P(S_T \mid S_M) = 0.80$$

Multiply along the path to obtain the joint probability for Monday and Tuesday:
$$P(S_M \cap S_T) = 0.70 \times 0.80 = 0.56 = \frac{14}{25}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Multiply branch probabilities P(Mon Sunny) * P(Tue Sunny | Mon Sunny) = 0.70 * 0.80.

parts.label: b
hints: Find the total probability that Tuesday is Sunny: $P(S_T) = P(S_M \cap S_T) + P(R_M \cap S_T)$.
Tuesday Rainy has probability $P(R_T) = 1 - 0.65 = 0.35$.
Wednesday Sunny follows from either a Sunny Tuesday or a Rainy Tuesday: $(0.65 \times 0.80) + (0.35 \times 0.30)$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the probability of each weather state on Tuesday:
$$P(S_T) = (0.70 \times 0.80) + (0.30 \times 0.30) = 0.56 + 0.09 = 0.65, \quad P(R_T) = 1 - 0.65 = 0.35$$

Set up the total probability for Wednesday Sunny:
$$P(S_W) = P(S_T)P(S_W \mid S_T) + P(R_T)P(S_W \mid R_T) = (0.65 \times 0.80) + (0.35 \times 0.30)$$

Evaluate the numerical sum:
$$P(S_W) = 0.52 + 0.105 = 0.625$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Determine the marginal distribution of weather outcomes on Tuesday:
$$P(S_T) = (0.70 \times 0.80) + (0.30 \times 0.30) = 0.65, \quad P(R_T) = 0.35$$

Propagate the probabilities to Wednesday using the Chapman-Kolmogorov transition structure:
$$P(S_W) = (0.65 \times 0.80) + (0.35 \times 0.30)$$

Compute the combined total probability for Wednesday:
$$P(S_W) = 0.52 + 0.105 = 0.625 = \frac{5}{8}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Calculate Tuesday weather probabilities: P(Tue Sunny) = (0.70 * 0.80) + (0.30 * 0.30) = 0.56 + 0.09 = 0.65, and P(Tue Rainy) = 0.35.
Apply total probability to Wednesday: P(Wed Sunny) = (0.65 * 0.80) + (0.35 * 0.30).

parts.label: c
hints: Apply Bayes theorem or conditional probability: $P(S_M \mid S_W) = \frac{P(S_M \cap S_W)}{P(S_W)}$.
From part (b), the denominator is $P(S_W) = 0.625$.
Find the numerator by summing all 3-day paths starting with $S_M$ and ending with $S_W$: $(S, S, S)$ and $(S, R, S)$.
Calculate: $P(S, S, S) = 0.70 \times 0.80 \times 0.80 = 0.448$ and $P(S, R, S) = 0.70 \times 0.20 \times 0.30 = 0.042$.

walkthrough.text:
Identify the paths starting Sunny on Monday and ending Sunny on Wednesday:
$$P(S_M \cap S_T \cap S_W) = 0.70 \times 0.80 \times 0.80 = 0.448, \quad P(S_M \cap R_T \cap S_W) = 0.70 \times 0.20 \times 0.30 = 0.042$$

Sum these paths to find the joint probability:
$$P(S_M \cap S_W) = 0.448 + 0.042 = 0.490$$

Evaluate the conditional probability using the result from part (b):
$$P(S_M \mid S_W) = \frac{P(S_M \cap S_W)}{P(S_W)} = \frac{0.490}{0.625} = \frac{98}{125} = 0.784$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Sum the probabilities of the two paths originating from a Sunny Monday that terminate in a Sunny Wednesday:
$$P(S_M \cap S_W) = (0.70 \times 0.80 \times 0.80) + (0.70 \times 0.20 \times 0.30) = 0.448 + 0.042 = 0.490$$

Formulate the conditional probability definition with the prior total probability from part (b):
$$P(S_M \mid S_W) = \frac{P(S_M \cap S_W)}{P(S_W)} = \frac{0.490}{0.625}$$

Simplify the fraction to find the final posterior probability:
$$P(S_M \mid S_W) = \frac{490}{625} = \frac{98}{125} = 0.784$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identify the two paths where Monday is Sunny and Wednesday is Sunny: (S, S, S) and (S, R, S).

parts.label: a
hints: If Green is transferred, Jar 2 has $3 + 1 = 4$ green counters and 5 white counters, giving 9 counters in total.
For two green counters without replacement, multiply $\frac{4}{9} \times \frac{3}{8}$.
If White is transferred, Jar 2 has 3 green counters and $5 + 1 = 6$ white counters, giving 9 counters in total.
For two green counters in this second scenario, multiply $\frac{3}{9} \times \frac{2}{8}$.

walkthrough.text:
Analyze Jar 2 after a green counter is transferred:
$$\text{Jar 2 has } 4G, 5W \text{ (total 9)} \implies P(GG \mid G_{\text{trans}}) = \frac{4}{9} \times \frac{3}{8} = \frac{12}{72} = \frac{1}{6}$$

Analyze Jar 2 after a white counter is transferred:
$$\text{Jar 2 has } 3G, 6W \text{ (total 9)} \implies P(GG \mid W_{\text{trans}}) = \frac{3}{9} \times \frac{2}{8} = \frac{6}{72} = \frac{1}{12}$$

State both established conditional values:
$$P(GG \mid G_{\text{trans}}) = \frac{1}{6}, \quad P(GG \mid W_{\text{trans}}) = \frac{1}{12}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Evaluate the product of branch probabilities following a green counter addition:
$$P(GG \mid G_{\text{trans}}) = \frac{4}{9} \times \frac{3}{8} = \frac{12}{72} = \frac{1}{6}$$

Evaluate the product of branch probabilities following a white counter addition:
$$P(GG \mid W_{\text{trans}}) = \frac{3}{9} \times \frac{2}{8} = \frac{6}{72} = \frac{1}{12}$$

Summarize the two conditional branch probabilities for the second stage:
$$P(GG \mid G_{\text{trans}}) = \frac{1}{6}, \quad P(GG \mid W_{\text{trans}}) = \frac{1}{12}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Update Jar 2 contents after green transfer (4 green, 5 white, total 9) and calculate (4/9) * (3/8).
Update Jar 2 contents after white transfer (3 green, 6 white, total 9) and obtain P(GG | White transferred) = (3/9) * (2/8) = 6/72 = 1/12.

parts.label: b
hints: Find the initial transfer probabilities from Jar 1: $P(G) = 4/6 = 2/3$ and $P(W) = 2/6 = 1/3$.
Use the conditional probabilities calculated in part (a): $1/6$ and $1/12$.
Apply the law of total probability: $P(GG) = P(G)P(GG \mid G) + P(W)P(GG \mid W)$.
Calculate $\left(\frac{2}{3} \times \frac{1}{6}\right) + \left(\frac{1}{3} \times \frac{1}{12}\right) = \frac{1}{9} + \frac{1}{36}$.

walkthrough.text:
Determine the transfer probabilities from Jar 1:
$$P(G_{\text{trans}}) = \frac{4}{6} = \frac{2}{3}, \quad P(W_{\text{trans}}) = \frac{2}{6} = \frac{1}{3}$$

Set up the total probability sum across both paths:
